beliefs: f(x) reverses x, then inserts 'I' at index ceil(len(x)/2) of the reversed string (i.e. just after the middle for odd lengths, at the middle for even lengths) [E3, E4, E5, E6]
For odd-length strings the 'I' sits just after the middle of the reversed string, e.g. 'abc'->'cbIa', 'abcde'->'edcIba' [E3, E4, E5]
For even-length strings the 'I' sits at the middle index of the reversed string, e.g. 'abcd'->'dcIba' [E3, E4]
All characters (case, digits, symbols, spaces, tabs) are preserved and reversed unchanged [E1, E2, E6]
Output length equals len(x)+1, so 'I' is inserted, not replacing [E4, E6]

The insertion index is computed from the reversed string's length, which equals len(x); for spaces this gives e.g. 'a b'->'bIa'? but E7/E8 observed 'Ia b' and 'Iba c', which contradicts this rule for strings with spaces [E7, E8]
